title: feat(plugin-audit, spec): audit checkpoints verify ES256 beside Ed25519, and a host signer pins the local keys
body:
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9SL6EvAc1d8R7MJH2esNU2M)_ Fixes #34165 Fixes #34166 Clause-②: yes (widening) Metadata-protocol: none ## 维护者速读 - 改了什么：审计封印的签名器接缝除 Ed25519 外接受 ES256(P-256),算法由可信公钥的类型决定，记录里不带算法字段;主机签名器接管后，旧本地钥签的历史靠它「钉住旧公钥」继续可信。 - 为什么改：Azure Key Vault 签不了 Ed25519,cloud#4128 的 Azure 客户无法把签名移进自己的 KMS;换签名器那天旧历史又会整体读成 untrusted_key。按你 11-16 的两条裁决做。 - 风险与回滚：只放宽验证端，Ed25519 指纹、本地签名器、证明包 v1 都不变，旧链照旧验过;新增「公钥字节须哈希到 key id」对所有锚生效(本地锚本来就满足)。回滚=revert 本 PR。 - 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signature.ts`(两种编码、失败即拒)、`verifier.ts` 的 `SigningKeyTrust`、`docs/adr/0154-…md` 末尾的修订节。 - 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-verifier.test.ts`,应见 54 passed,含 ES256 与「钉住旧公钥」两组新用例。 - 需要你做的：本 PR 改了 ADR(Tier H),请在审核席核过后批准合入。 ## What changes **#34165 — ES256 beside Ed25519 (ADR-0154 D4, amended; ruling 6909369413).** - New internal module `plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signature.ts`, the one place a trusted key is parsed and a signature checked. The closed pair is Ed25519 and ES256. The algorithm is the trusted key's type. Records carry no algorithm field. - The ruling left three points to this card. This PR fixes them as follows: - **ES256 key id**: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the key's DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, P-256, point uncompressed (91 bytes). Ed25519 keeps the SHA-256 of its raw 32 bytes. So the key id binds the type, and for ES256 the curve too. `SigningKeyTrust` now refuses any key whose bytes do not hash to the id it was asked under, for every anchor. The local anchor and the offline bundle check already enforced this. A host anchor did not. - **Signature encoding**: `r || s`, 64 bytes (IEEE P1363). This is the JWS form that the name ES256 denotes (RFC 7518 §3.4), and what Azure Key Vault returns. AWS KMS and Vault transit return DER by default, so their signer converts before returning. A DER signature never verifies. - **Explicit key-type check**: the key must be raw 32 bytes (Ed25519) or a P-256 SPKI that re-encodes to exactly the bytes given. Anything else fails closed as `untrusted_key`: P-384, RSA, a compressed point, an Ed25519 key in SPKI form, or base64 that does not round-trip. - `verifier.ts` (`SigningKeyTrust`, the one admission rule for the live check, the offline check and the redaction amendment writer) and `bundle.ts` (offline key admission) now go through it. - The bundle format stays `objectstack.audit.proof-bundle.v1`. An older reader sees an ES256 key as untrusted, which is the fail-closed direction. **#34166 — a host signer pins the local keys (ADR-0154 D6, amended; ruling 6909375840).** The ruling adds no fallback and exports nothing. So the framework change is the contract text in the `trustedPublicKey` docblock, the ADR note (including that a host may destroy the wrapped legacy private half at the switch), and the test the ruling names. **Contract and record.** - `packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`: docblocks only. No type or export changes. They cover the two algorithms, the key-id and encoding rules, and the host signer's pinning duty. - `docs/adr/0154-…md`: a dated amendment section for D4 and D6, with pointers at D4's signature bullet, D6's seam bullet and the status line. - `packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts`: docblock and fingerprint comment only. The CLI already passes the host signer as the anchor and the `--trusted-key` fingerprints as given, and neither path is algorithm-specific. ## Tests All new cases sit in the shared verifier harness, `audit-seal-verifier.test.ts`, as two top-level `describe`s. Every live run there is also re-judged offline from its proof bundle (`--bundle --trusted-key`) and must give the same report. - An ES256 host signer seals a ledger. It verifies live under the signer's anchor and offline under its fingerprint. The bundle carries the key as SPKI under the SHA-256 of those bytes. - A forged ES256 signature fails, and that checkpoint holds nothing. - The DER encoding of a valid ES256 signature fails. - A record signed by a P-384, RSA, compressed-P-256 or Ed25519-SPKI key that the anchor answers for is `untrusted_key` (four cases). - An Ed25519 signature, also 64 bytes, never verifies under an EC key. - A key answered under an id its bytes do not hash to is `untrusted_key`. - **#34166, as the ruling names it**: 1. A local-sealed chain is built, and its `--out` bundle's keys become the host signer's pins. 2. The ES256 host signer seals the next window on the same chains. 3. All six rows verify, live and offline, under both keys. 4. A key planted after the switch (its wrapped half opens, so D6's own derivation would trust it) re-signs a checkpoint and reads `untrusted_key` under the host anchor. - A companion case: a host signer with no pins reads the local key's checkpoints `untrusted_key`. No existing test changed. ## Acceptance notes - The ADR amendment makes this PR **Tier H**: it lands only on an approval from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`. - **Done-when, live `os audit verify` with a registered ES256 signer**: proven at the plugin layer through `verifyAuditLedger({ trust })`, the function the CLI's live path calls with `kernel.getService('audit.checkpointSigner')`. The CLI code is unchanged apart from comments, and no CLI spawn test registers a host signer. That would need a host-signer plugin in a stack fixture, and this PR adds none. - The amendment writer reads trust through the same `SigningKeyTrust` and `anchoredPublicKeyOf`. So it admits ES256 checkpoints the same way, and it is not separately pinned here. ## Verification All readings were taken at head `6a9dffba` (`origin/main` `24b6ae55` merged in), in this branch's worktree. - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` + `typecheck`: lock VERDICT command-exit 0, **Test Files 99/99, Tests 1665/1665**. `audit-seal-verifier.test.ts` alone: 54/54. - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && … check:generated`: "All 14 generated artifacts are up to date". `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0. - `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 100 derived families, all run, each `:: exit 0`. `--ran`: "100 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 100 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED". Five families first exited 3 on a missing build prerequisite or a pinned control commit outside the shallow clone. They were re-run green after `turbo run build` of their named closure and a fetch of that commit.
Ablations (each through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs: the mutation proven on disk, restored to the HEAD blob f929f9a51bc1, git diff HEAD empty) The test imports `signature.ts` from source, so no build sits between the mutation and the run. 1. **Delete the key-id binding** (`sha256(bytes) !== keyId → null`): red, 2/54. Failing: "trusts no key the anchor answers under an id its bytes do not hash to" and the existing "trusts a key the bundle carries only when it hashes to the fingerprint given". 2. **Admit Ed25519 only** (the behaviour before this PR): red, 10/54. Every ES256 case fails, and so does the #34166 switch case. 3. **Accept a DER ES256 signature** (drop the 64-byte check and pick the encoding by length): red, 1/54. Failing: "refuses a valid ES256 signature in DER encoding". - A first attempt that kept the length check stayed green, 54/54. The length check alone refuses DER, so that mutation removed nothing the test depends on. The re-run anchored on both lines.
